claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake and drop an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, before it ever starts.

In CodePipeline `SUPERSEDED` mode, if a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting CodePipeline execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each runs in turn.
CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType`).
The AWS CLI `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set `executionMode` and `pipelineType` for a pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The link /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ exists as the aws.codepipeline.Pipeline resource documentation.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that a deployment job targets, which can prevent concurrent runs from reaching the same stack.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a stage-level property that controls how the exclusive lock check on a referenced environment behaves.
The Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` property defaults to `runLatest`, and also accepts `sequential`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled) rather than eventually run.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage runs against the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack one at a time.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has an `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ describing update conflicts.
A registry page exists at /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/.

When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
TeamCity's build configuration advanced option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0 (unlimited).
The 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is located under the build configuration's General Settings in TeamCity.
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 causes a second build to be queued behind the first and run only after the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior.
Link target exists: /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ page on update conflicts.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job serializes deployments to that environment.
In Azure Pipelines, `lockBehavior: sequential` is set on the stage so that deployments run sequentially with an exclusive lock check.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section anchored at #serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
In AWS CodePipeline, the default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
